research_goal:
  id: GOAL-NISTSEED-ab8949
  title: >-
    Reconstruct the commonality behind eleven omitted NIST/ANSI prime-field
    curve candidates without mistaking bounded implementation behavior for a
    historical or cryptanalytic conclusion
  objective: >-
    Pursue exhaustively the commonality behind the eleven reconstructed omitted
    NIST/ANSI prime-field curve candidates. Preserve the complete candidate
    universe, public seed and draft provenance, field-matched published controls,
    and every negative, censored, failed, or inconclusive result. Determine,
    within explicitly bounded evidence, whether a source-identified historical
    acceptance/selection procedure or a prospectively predictive and independently
    validated property explains the omissions. The recovered ECPP V3.4.1 path is
    one possible behavioral discriminator only. Running it, building its runner,
    or observing a 21-order split never by itself completes this goal, establishes
    historical use, or establishes a cryptographic weakness.
  question_ids:
    - RQ-NISTSEED-ac8851
  active_hypothesis_ids: []
  status: active
  runtime:
    provider: none
    goal_id: null
  campaign_budget:
    maximum_batches: null
    total_wall_clock_seconds: null
    max_concurrent: 1
  current_batch_id: BATCH-08d006
  dispatch_queue_path: coordination/goals/GOAL-NISTSEED-ab8949/batches/BATCH-08d006/dispatch_queue.json
  open_batches: []
  scope_boundary:
    owns: >-
      Historical/public reconstruction of the NIST/ANSI prime-field candidate
      stream, including the eleven reconstructed omissions, the field-matched
      published controls, candidate-generation and acceptance predicates, public
      seed/draft/source provenance, and bounded replays of recovered period
      software when their full configuration, trace, certificate, and censoring
      conditions are frozen before execution.
    not_owned:
      GOAL-ECDLP2M-001: >-
        Characteristic-two ECDLP index calculus, descent cost, standardized
        binary curves, and the NISTBIN subarea. Nothing in this goal changes,
        reuses, or interprets that lane.
      GOAL-PFDR-fd09e0: >-
        Prime-field point-decomposition and degree-of-regularity research. This
        goal does not infer ECDLP complexity, recovery, or a solver advantage.
      GOAL-SCURVE-9f5556: >-
        General SafeCurves-style implementation and parameter audits. This goal
        is limited to the named historical NIST/ANSI omission reconstruction.
  claim_boundary: >-
    Observations are descriptive program behavior under the exact recovered
    artifact, inputs and controls. A valid legacy certificate is software
    admission evidence, while independent primality evidence remains a separate
    bound input. A timeout, crash, malformed output, missing completion, or
    checker refusal is censored/INDETERMINATE for mathematical classification.
    No result implies a hidden weakness, historical use of the artifact, a 1997
    runtime, an ECDLP advantage, or an explanation of the omissions without the
    separately stated evidence.
  completion_criteria:
    - >-
      A committed, independently reviewed record identifies a historically
      sourced candidate-generation or acceptance procedure and reproducibly
      accounts for the eleven omissions and retained controls across its declared
      candidate domain, including every stated exception and uncertainty.
    - >-
      Or, a committed, independently reviewed predictive property is frozen
      before its decisive holdout evaluation, is measured with matched controls
      and complete censoring, and accounts for the omissions over an explicitly
      stated domain without being presented as historical use or a security claim
      unless independent historical or cryptanalytic evidence separately supports
      that stronger conclusion.
    - >-
      The conclusion records the remaining unvisited/censored candidate domain,
      source-provenance limits, alternative explanations, and any successor
      condition. A tooling task, compatibility control, approved protocol,
      ECPP pass/failure, or bounded run alone is insufficient.
  pause_conditions:
    - >-
      Original source, caller, trace, or verification material is unavailable;
      record the precise missing artifact and a recheck route as an impediment
      while the goal remains active.
    - >-
      A compatibility runtime, frozen protocol, archive binding, or independent
      review is unavailable or invalid; this is an implementation/infrastructure
      impediment, never a conclusion about the omission mechanism.
  impediments:
    - id: IMP-NISTSEED-ECPP-RUNNER
      raised: '2026-10-24'
      condition: >-
        The recovered ECPP compatibility library has only a describe-only public
        interface and lacks a supervisor-callable fail-closed runner/checker.
      what_is_blocked: >-
        A lawful scientific 21-order ECPP comparison packet and any interpretation
        of named-order behavior.
      clears_when: >-
        TASK-20261024-4f1bf4 produces and TASK-20261024-b17301 archives the
        source-bound zero-run runner/checker package; a later Coordinator then
        completes a separate review-required experiment packet.
      recheck: >-
        Read the archive receipt for TASK-20261024-b17301, verify its source
        hashes, then assess a new prospective packet with
        tools/experiment_preapproval.py.
      asserts_nothing_about: >-
        Whether ECPP distinguishes any candidate, why the eleven candidates were
        omitted, historical use, or cryptographic security.
  next_action: >-
    Open BATCH-08d006 as the zero-run implementation lane under
    DEC-20261024-46d623; claim and complete TASK-20261024-4f1bf4, then archive
    it with TASK-20261024-b17301. A distinct Coordinator design task follows;
    no scientific ECPP order is authorized by this batch.
  owner: coordinator
  created_at: '2026-10-24'
  updated_at: '2026-10-24'

research_question:
  id: RQ-NISTSEED-ac8851
  title: >-
    What commonality, if any, explains the eleven reconstructed omitted NIST/ANSI
    prime-field curve candidates while distinguishing source provenance, observed
    software behavior, mathematical properties, and cryptanalytic relevance?
  scope:
    curve_families:
      - >-
        The eleven reconstructed omitted prime-field NIST/ANSI seed classes and
        their full curve UIDs in research/nist_seed_ecpp_compat_20261024/cohort-inputs.json.
      - >-
        The ten frozen published controls: eight same-field controls plus the
        P-384 and P-521 larger-field controls.
      - >-
        The broader reconstructed candidate/acceptance corpus only when a later
        protocol names it before execution; no expansion is implied by this
        opening record.
    field_types:
      - Prime fields F_p for the frozen NIST/ANSI candidate/control cohort.
    bit_sizes:
      - Prime-field candidate sizes represented in the frozen cohort, including
        the P-384 and P-521 scale controls.
    methods:
      - >-
        Source-bound reconstruction of public drafts, candidate-generation and
        acceptance procedures, with original-caller and period provenance kept
        distinct from later source availability.
      - >-
        Bounded, fail-closed replay of recovered public software only after a
        frozen protocol binds inputs, catalog, RNG, machine protections,
        certificates, raw traces, censoring, and independent checks.
      - >-
        Prospectively preregistered structural or behavioral discriminators with
        matched controls, a holdout before interpretation, and explicit limits on
        historical and cryptanalytic transfer.
  motivation: >-
    Eleven reconstructed omissions from the NIST/ANSI prime-field candidate stream
    remain unexplained. Existing public-source and bounded structural screens narrow
    individual explanations but do not identify the historical selector. The
    recovered ECPP artifact is period-available software with a source-inspected
    conditional false-composite path, but no named cohort order has run and period
    availability is not caller provenance. A durable question must hold the full
    user objective rather than treating one compatibility replay as the answer.
  decision_target: >-
    A committed Coordinator synthesis, after the required independent review, that
    states whether the tested evidence supports a source-identified procedure, a
    predictive property with an explicit domain, or neither; lists all remaining
    alternatives and uncensored/censored candidate scope; and separately labels any
    claim about historical use, software behavior, group security, or ECDLP
    relevance. No bounded ECPP result is sufficient by itself.
  constraints:
    - >-
      Preserve the eleven omitted classes, eight same-field published controls,
      and P-384/P-521 controls unless a future additive protocol explicitly
      creates a separately labeled extension.
    - >-
      No historical-attribution claim without actual caller, invocation, log, or
      comparable period provenance. Availability of code, a later source archive,
      or a modern compatibility build is not historical-use evidence.
    - >-
      No curve weakness, ECDLP advantage, key-recovery, or runtime-era claim from
      a software label, exit code, certificate, timeout, crash, or control alone.
    - >-
      A timeout, crash, missing completion, malformed certificate, or checker
      refusal is an implementation observation and censored/INDETERMINATE for the
      mathematical classification; preserve all raw artifacts.
    - >-
      A proposed separator is frozen before its decisive holdout, uses matched
      controls, and reports all failures and exceptions. A result on the original
      cohort is not independent replication.
    - >-
      This question is distinct from RQ-NISTBIN-06157b: it studies prime-field
      NIST/ANSI historical candidate selection, not binary-field ECDLP/index
      calculus.
  status: active
  owner: coordinator
  goal_id: GOAL-NISTSEED-ab8949
  created_at: '2026-10-24'
  related_problem: problems/nist-seed-selection-rule-unexplained.md

    - >-
      The smallest valid corrective action is a zero-run implementation lane with

    - >-
      The broader goal completion criteria preserve the original user objective:

  evidence_refs: []
